name: ACP PaymentManager releasePayment double release (claim tracked in memory)
summary: PaymentManager.releasePayment loads the job into memory, increments amountClaimed on that copy only and has its escrow-sufficiency check commented out, so every call pays the full job budget again out of the pooled escrow. ACPRouter releases payment automatically when a job reaches COMPLETED and also lets anyone call claimBudget on a completed job. From block 37590595 one EOA's claimBudget calls re-paid 1,408 already-settled jobs; on 2026-03-02 an attacker created a 97,000 USDC job with its own provider, completed it and claimed it a second time, and copycats followed until the implementation was replaced.
notes: UUPS upgrade of the PaymentManager proxy from its initial implementation 0x8e4fa97e4e8d0b8618065809197e1bbf4fab19ab to PaymentManager 0x56c3af6c; the next upgrade (0x536823c8, block 42834676) is the post-attack fix.

Each component is the USDC that PaymentManager transferred out (platform fee, evaluator fee and provider amount) in releases of a job beyond its first release: 1,865 re-releases before the attack (1,408 jobs, all sent by 0x7346dc42102b5cdba321d587564612d1f3878ad2), the attack's second 97,000 USDC release, and 49 re-releases in 7 transactions by four senders afterwards. Fees paid to the platform treasury are not deducted; the attacker's own 97,000 USDC budget, which funded the first release of its job, is not counted. USDC valued at par.

ACPRouter (proxy 0xa6c9ba866992cfd7fd6460ba912bfa405ada9df0, implementation 0x71d4d6a3f588d1ea440a5e681ecb52d53c3d255a at the anchor, later 0x7ae45990 and 0x307e34d9) supplies the two release paths (automatic release on COMPLETED and permissionless claimBudget) but holds no claim state; it is recorded as the entry point, not as a second target. Its upgrades at blocks 42827279 and 42827451 only tightened phase-jump rules (source-3 diff) and postdate the anchor.
